proposed_title: Apply the federal trust responsibility and treaty-reserved rights to environmental and land management decisions
description: Identifies which Tribal nations hold treaty-reserved, statutory or Executive-order rights (hunting, fishing, gathering, water, access) in a project or planning area; analyzes how proposed actions affect the exercise of those rights; and designs measures that accommodate them. Observable: written rights analysis in the decision record; plan components that provide access and avoid restricting treaty uses except under the applicable legal test.
subsector: cross-subsector (land, water, fisheries, wildlife, energy siting)
rationale: Plans already require it: 102 treaty/reserved-right components in 39 plans, e.g., NWFP Aquatic Conservation Strategy 1994 'American Indian Uses' restriction test; Nez Perce-Clearwater 2025 FW-DC-TT-09 access for treaty-reserved rights. v1 mentions treaty rights only in a sector note. This is knowledge about federal law and obligations, appropriate for the project to define.

proposed_title: Conduct government-to-government consultation with Tribal nations as a pre-decisional process
description: Determines when an action has Tribal implications; invites Tribal leadership early, with adequate notice and materials, and with officials who hold decision authority present; seeks consensus where policy requires; keeps and shares a record of consultation; explains how Tribal input changed or did not change the decision; continues consultation through implementation. Observable: consultation plan, invitation timing, attendance of decision-makers, record shared with the Tribe, response-to-input documentation.
rationale: Rewrite of 6.5.1 with observable behaviors drawn from current agency policy (NPS DO 71C: 30-day notice, record within 10 business days; DOI 2022: early, pre-decisional, consensus-seeking, staff training before participation). Tribes in the 2025 USWFS consultation criticized webinars presented as consultation - the competency must distinguish consultation from notification. Transforming because procedural floors are moving (OMB M-25-36; Part 800 NPRM).

proposed_title: Protect confidential Tribal information across records systems, disclosure law and AI tools
description: Before receiving information from a Tribe, explains what records and disclosure laws (FOIA, state public-records acts) could compel the organization to release and what exemptions exist (e.g., NHPA s.304, ARPA) without overstating protection; withholds sensitive site locations from maps, reports and datasets; keeps Tribal information out of third-party AI and cloud tools unless the Tribe authorizes it; applies the Tribe's handling instructions. Observable: disclosure briefing documented; redaction/holdback log; AI-use authorization on file.
rationale: 301 DM 7 tells staff not to overstate confidentiality given FOIA limits; NPS will not record culturally sensitive information without permission; plans carry NHPA s.304 confidentiality standards (Mt Baker-Snoqualmie 1990; Umatilla 1990). v1 exposure coding treats documentation of Tribal input and cultural-site mapping as AI-augmentable without any governance condition, which makes this an emerging, AI-driven need.

proposed_title: Structure and administer agreements with Tribal governments for shared or Tribally led stewardship
description: Selects and uses the right instrument for the purpose - self-determination contracts and self-governance compacts (ISDEAA/P.L. 93-638), cooperative agreements, MOUs, co-stewardship and co-management agreements, Tribal Forest Protection Act and Good Neighbor agreements with Tribes, data-sharing agreements - and administers them so that Tribal authority, funding and decision roles are honored. Observable: agreement drafted with roles, authorities, funding and dispute terms; inherently federal functions correctly reserved; performance and payment on schedule.
rationale: Fire and forestry already run through 638 contracts and compacts (three options per NIFC Ch.6); 400 co-stewardship agreements existed by Dec 2024; USWFS must build ISDEAA administration capacity; Tribes asked for formal agreements and advisory structures. Transforming because the policy footing shifted in 2025-26 (EO 14112 rescinded; Bears Ears Commission eliminated).

proposed_title: Operate within Tribal jurisdiction and Tribal law as a non-Tribal party
description: Recognizes when Tribal law and Tribal regulatory authority apply (e.g., Tribal codes, Tribal water quality standards under treatment-as-a-state, Tribal permits and cultural resource ordinances on Tribal lands, Tribal research codes) and complies with them; coordinates with the Tribal department that holds the authority. Observable: Tribal requirements identified in project scoping; Tribal approvals obtained where required.
rationale: v1 frames Tribes as parties to be consulted, never as governments whose law binds others. Tribal environmental programs build ordinances (e.g., Tribal air ordinance as an eligible CAA 103 activity; Tribal response program ordinances under CERCLA 128(a)). The July 2026 draft Part 800 would replace Tribal concurrence on Tribal-land discoveries with consultation, which makes knowing Tribal law more, not less, important. Label J because I did not read a source enumerating TAS approvals.

proposed_title: Support Tribally led cultural and prescribed fire as a partner without directing Tribal knowledge
description: Removes administrative and operational barriers to Tribally led burning on lands the organization manages (planning, permitting, liability, resource ordering, smoke coordination, reimbursements) under agreements with the Tribe; defers objectives, methods and knowledge to Tribal fire practitioners; ensures qualification requirements do not exceed what the agreement specifies. Observable: barriers documented and resolved; agreement-based burn plans; timely reimbursement.
rationale: Tribes asked USWFS for basic cultural burning protocols, a Tribal consultation section in regional fire management plans and reduced barriers to Tribally led prescribed fire; California's 2021 strategy created a grant program for Tribal cultural burning. Replaces v1's recommendation to credential Indigenous fire stewardship: the competency describes the partner's conduct, not the knowledge.

proposed_title: Govern data about Tribal lands, resources and peoples under Tribal authority (CARE alongside FAIR)
description: Identifies when a monitoring, research or analytics activity generates data about Tribal lands, resources, citizens or knowledge; establishes before collection, with the Tribe's data authority, who owns, accesses, publishes, retains and can withdraw the data; applies CARE alongside FAIR; uses Local Contexts Notices where appropriate; honors repatriation and deletion requests. Observable: signed data agreement predating collection; metadata carrying Tribal terms; withdrawal executed when requested.
rationale: Revision of 7.1.1 for non-Tribal professionals. Monitoring partnerships are a common co-stewardship form (Mashpee Wampanoag review of offshore wind environmental data). CARE and Local Contexts details are from prior knowledge (TN-060, TN-061 not re-read this session) - re-verify before publication. Publication gated on Tribal review (P-TN-03).

proposed_title: Administer federal or state funding to Tribal governments in ways that respect self-governance
description: Structures awards and agreements to minimize reporting burden, pays and reimburses on time, supports recurring and compactable funding where authorized, includes staffing costs in base funding, and involves Tribes in formula and budget development. Observable: payment cycle times; reporting requirements justified; Tribal input in formula design documented.
subsector: grants and financial assistance; fire; forestry; environmental programs
rationale: What Tribal employers asked for: reimbursement backlogs (about $8.6M Santa Ynez Band of Chumash since 2019; about $3M Karuk); 'project-by-project funding is not sustainable'; IFMAT IV: base funding should cover staffing at GS-equivalent pay before project funds grow; Congress members cite reporting burdens. This is the federal side of Tribal workforce stability.

proposed_title: Apply Indian preference and Tribal employment rights lawfully in hiring for positions serving Tribal lands
description: Knows where Indian preference applies (statutory federal preference for BIA/IHS; Tribal preference ordinances and TERO requirements on Tribal lands; preference provisions in self-determination agreements) and applies it as a political classification; designs recruitment so preference does not leave positions vacant (e.g., pathways for preference hires from other disciplines). Observable: compliant announcements; documented preference determinations; bridging training plans.
rationale: Tribes asked USWFS to apply Indian preference across roles serving Tribal lands as a political classification; IFMAT IV finding C4 notes preference hiring increased Native foresters but some positions go unfilled or hires need NASP preparation. Coordinate with FH (federal hiring) - I am not proposing FH's lane, only flagging the competency.

proposed_title: Engage with Indigenous knowledge only on its holders' terms
description: Recognizes that Indigenous knowledge belongs to and is interpreted by its holders; asks the Tribe's governance structure who may share knowledge and under what conditions; obtains free, prior and informed consent before receiving it; uses it only for the purpose agreed; attributes it as the holder specifies (including not at all); compensates time and services without claiming ownership; declines to characterize, summarize or generalize it beyond what is authorized. Observable: consent record; purpose limitation in agreement; attribution as specified; no unauthorized reuse.
rationale: Replaces v1 5.3.2. The competency concerns the professional's conduct, which is the project's to describe; it does not define or rank Indigenous knowledge. Drawn from 301 DM 7 (FPIC before receipt; rely on Indigenous Peoples to interpret; IK inalienable; compensation does not transfer ownership) and NPS DO 71C. Requires Tribal advisory review before publication.

proposed_title: Coordinate cultural resource work with Tribal Historic Preservation Officers under Tribal direction
description: Engages THPOs and Tribal cultural monitors early in identification, evaluation and effects work; refers determinations of religious and cultural significance to Tribes; protects confidential site information; plans for post-review discoveries consistent with Tribal law on Tribal lands; maintains working relationships beyond individual undertakings. Observable: THPO engaged before identification fieldwork; referrals logged; confidentiality maintained.
subsector: cultural resources; NEPA/Section 106; energy and infrastructure siting
rationale: Rewrite of 5.3.3 task language. 129 plan components carry NHPA Section 106 touchpoints. The July 2026 draft Part 800 rewrite (pending OIRA) would reduce THPO roles and remove Tribal special-expertise language; practitioners who keep THPOs engaged early will be operating above a lowered floor. Transforming because the regulatory baseline is changing.

proposed_title: Sustain government-to-government obligations when procedural requirements change
description: Tracks changes to consultation, Section 106 and NEPA procedures (e.g., OMB M-25-36 presumptions; Part 800 rulemaking; post-Seven County NEPA practice; reorganizations such as USWFS) and distinguishes what remains required by treaty, statute, trust responsibility and Tribal law from what is procedural discretion; advises decision-makers on legal and relationship risk. Observable: change briefings; decision memos that separate obligations from discretion.
rationale: 2025-26 shows high procedural volatility (EO 14112 rescinded; M-25-36; USWFS; Bears Ears Commission eliminated; Part 800 NPRM). Practitioners in all actors need to keep obligations distinct from procedures. Proponent-side view (Hunton, TN-042) sees efficiency gains; Tribal organizations (NATHPO) see loss of meaningful consultation - the competency is neutral on the policy but requires knowing both.

proposed_title: Establish and sustain core environmental program capacity for a Tribal government
description: Builds and maintains the administrative, financial, information-management, baseline-assessment, public-education, legal and technical capacities a Tribal environmental program needs to plan, implement and, where the Tribe chooses, assume federal environmental programs; develops and updates an EPA-Tribal Environmental Plan (ETEP); manages multi-media work across water, air, waste and land with small staff. Observable: ETEP current; workplans meeting commitments; programs assumed or implemented as planned.
rationale: The only candidate here written FOR Tribal employees rather than for non-Tribal partners. It describes public-administration functions defined in EPA's public GAP framework, not Indigenous knowledge, so it is within scope - but it must be validated by Tribal environmental professionals (e.g., via Regional Tribal Operations Committees, ITEP) and carried in a Tribal-actor role variant only if they agree it reflects their work. FY26 priorities emphasize delegated programs and solid/hazardous waste.
